packs.title: Quick & Easy 10-Second Brain Warm-Up
packs.subtitle: 100% Easy instant-solve tasks across Math, Logic, Science, Chess & Words for fast unlocks
packs.author: QuizLock Fast-Flow Lab

questions.question: What is 15 + 12?
questions.explanation: 15 + 10 = 25, plus 2 more equals 27!
questions.hintText: Split 12 into 10 and 2, then add them one by one.

questions.question: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The day directly after Tuesday is Wednesday.
questions.hintText: Monday, Tuesday, ...?

questions.question: At what temperature (in °C) does liquid water boil into steam at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure.
questions.hintText: Think of a bubbling kettle. It is much hotter than a warm bath.

questions.question: White to move: Find the winning move to capture Black's undefended piece!
questions.explanation: 1. Rxd5 wins Black's Queen for free along the open d-file!
questions.hintText: Look along the open file: your Rook can take a piece nobody protects.

questions.question: Which word means the SAME as 'HAPPY'?
questions.explanation: 'Joyful' means full of happiness and delight.
questions.hintText: Think about how you feel on your birthday.

questions.question: What number does print(5 + 5) show on the screen?
questions.explanation: 5 + 5 adds the two numbers together and prints 10.
questions.hintText: The computer adds first, then shows the result.

questions.question: What is 25 + 35?
questions.hintText: Add the tens first, then the ones.

questions.question: 2, 4, 8, 16, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: Powers of 2: 16 x 2 = 32.
questions.hintText: Double each number.

questions.question: What is the brightest star seen from Earth during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and it is so close to Earth that it outshines every other star.
questions.hintText: It lights up our day!

questions.question: What is a synonym for 'tiny'?
questions.explanation: Tiny means very small.
questions.hintText: Think of a tiny insect.

questions.question: Which piece can move backward, forward, and sideways any number of squares?
questions.explanation: The Rook moves horizontally and vertically any distance.
questions.hintText: It goes in straight lines and never diagonally.

questions.question: In Python, what is len('Cat')?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' has 3 characters: C, a, t.
questions.hintText: Count the letters in Cat.

questions.question: What is 12 x 5?
questions.hintText: Split 12 into 10 and 2, multiply each by 5, then add.

questions.question: There are 3 apples on a table and you take 2 of them. How many apples do you have now?
questions.explanation: You took 2 apples, so you have 2 apples!
questions.hintText: Look at the apples in YOUR hands, not on the table.

questions.question: What kind of energy does a moving car possess?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is energy of motion.
questions.hintText: The faster the car goes, the more of this energy it has.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'Victory'?
questions.explanation: Defeat is the opposite of victory.
questions.hintText: Think of how the losing team feels at the end of the game.

questions.question: What is 48 / 6?
questions.hintText: Count by 6s up to 48.

questions.question: Which of these can a pawn promote to when it reaches the 8th rank?
questions.explanation: A pawn can promote to a Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight.
questions.hintText: Promotion is a reward: your pawn becomes a strong piece.

questions.question: Which symbol is used for comments in Python?
questions.explanation: # denotes a single-line comment in Python.
questions.hintText: Look for the sign shaped like a tic-tac-toe grid.

questions.question: If you face North and turn 90 degrees clockwise, which way do you face?
questions.explanation: Turning clockwise from North points to East.
questions.hintText: Clockwise is to the right, like the hands of a clock.

questions.question: Can sound travel through a vacuum (empty space)?
questions.optionsString: Yes|No|Only in zero gravity|Faster than in air
questions.explanation: Sound requires a medium (air, water, solid) to vibrate.
questions.hintText: Sound is a shaking that passes from one particle to the next.

questions.question: What is 9 squared (9 x 9)?
questions.explanation: 9 x 10 = 90, and one 9 less is 90 - 9 = 81.
questions.hintText: Try 9 x 10 first, then take away one 9.

questions.question: Which of these is a compound word?
questions.explanation: Sun + light = Sunlight.
questions.hintText: Like football = foot + ball. Which word splits into two words?

questions.question: What is it called when the King is attacked and cannot escape?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends the game with a win for the attacker.
questions.hintText: The ultimate goal in chess.

questions.question: In code, what is an ordered collection of items called?
questions.explanation: A list (or array) stores ordered elements.
questions.hintText: Think of a row of numbered boxes, one item in each.

questions.question: A square has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 x 5 cm = 20 cm.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 sides.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a mammal?
questions.explanation: An eagle is a bird, while dolphins and whales are mammals.
questions.hintText: Mammals feed milk to their babies. Which one doesn't?

questions.question: How does heat travel from the Sun to Earth across space?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation travels through empty vacuum.
questions.hintText: Space is empty, so nothing can carry the heat. Think of light.

questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' is the correct spelling.
questions.hintText: It begins like the word 'define'.

questions.question: What is 50% of 84?
questions.hintText: 50% is the same as one half.

questions.question: Which two pieces participate in castling?
questions.optionsString: King and Queen|King and Rook|Bishop and Knight|Rook and Pawn
questions.explanation: Castling is a special move involving King and Rook.
questions.hintText: The other piece is the one standing in the corner of the board.

questions.question: What does the % (modulo) operator calculate?
questions.explanation: Modulo returns the remainder (e.g. 7 % 3 = 1).
questions.hintText: Share 10 sweets between 3 kids. Look at the sweets left over.

questions.question: How many seconds are in 3 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 x 60 = 180 seconds.
questions.hintText: 60 seconds in 1 minute.

packs.title: Tweens & Middle School (10–13 yrs): Smart STEM & Logic
packs.subtitle: Grades 5–8 percentages, speed & distance, solar eclipses, sequences & Python loops
packs.author: QuizLock STEM Academy

questions.question: What is 25% (one quarter) of 100?
questions.hintText: A quarter means 4 equal parts. Split 100 into 4 groups.

questions.question: A train travels at a steady speed of 60 km/h for 2 hours. How many kilometers does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance d = v × t = 60 km/h × 2 h = 120 km.
questions.hintText: The train covers 60 km every hour. How many such hours are there?

questions.question: What number comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
questions.hintText: Find what you do to 3 to get 6, then to 6 to get 12.

questions.question: What causes a Solar Eclipse on Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth|Earth passes into Mars's shadow|The Sun turns off briefly|Clouds block the sky
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves directly between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth.
questions.hintText: It is about a shadow falling on Earth. Which object must stand in front of the Sun?

questions.question: What does the adjective 'BENEVOLENT' mean?
questions.optionsString: Kind and well-meaning|Extremely loud|Hostile and angry|Freezing cold
questions.explanation: From Latin 'bene' (well/good), 'benevolent' means kind, generous, and well-meaning.
questions.hintText: Latin root 'bene' means good or well.

questions.question: In Python, how many times does the loop `for i in range(5):` repeat?
questions.explanation: range(5) generates the 5 integers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — so the loop runs exactly 5 times.
questions.hintText: Write out the numbers range(5) gives, starting at 0, and count them.

questions.question: What is 3/4 + 1/8 expressed in eighths?
questions.explanation: Convert to common denominator: 3/4 = 6/8. Then 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.
questions.hintText: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 2 to get eighths.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth lies directly beneath the crust?
questions.explanation: The mantle is the thick silicate rock layer situated between Earth's crust and outer core.
questions.hintText: It makes up about 84% of Earth's total volume.

questions.question: What is the sum of the three interior angles of ANY triangle on a flat plane?
questions.explanation: On a flat Euclidean plane, the interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.
questions.hintText: Tear off the three corners of a paper triangle and line them up side by side.

questions.question: In Python, what is the index of the FIRST element in a list?
questions.explanation: In Python and most modern programming languages, array and list indexing starts at index 0.
questions.hintText: An index counts the items that come before it. How many come before the first?

questions.question: What is the scientific term when a solid turns directly into a gas without melting into liquid first?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the phase transition directly from solid to gas (like dry ice solid CO₂).
questions.hintText: Think of dry ice turning directly into smoke-like gas at room temperature.

questions.question: A model car has a scale ratio of 1:10. If the real car is 250 cm long, how long is the model car?
questions.explanation: Scale 1:10 means divide by 10: 250 cm / 10 = 25 cm.
questions.hintText: 1:10 means every 10 cm of the real car becomes 1 cm on the model.

questions.question: Which cellular organelle is often called the 'powerhouse of the cell' for producing ATP energy?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy (ATP) needed to power cell reactions.
questions.hintText: Muscle cells need lots of energy, so they are packed with these.

questions.question: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of 2x + 25?
questions.hintText: First solve for x by subtracting 5 from 20, then dividing by 3.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 60 grams and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = Mass / Volume = 60 g / 20 cm³ = 3 g/cm³.
questions.hintText: Density = how many grams sit in each 1 cm³. Share the mass over the volume.

questions.question: In Python, what does 'QuizLock'[0:4] evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Slice [0:4] takes characters at indices 0, 1, 2, and 3: 'Q', 'u', 'i', 'z'.
questions.hintText: A slice starts at index 0 and stops just before the end index.

questions.question: What is the area of a right-angled triangle with base 6 cm and height 8 cm?
questions.explanation: Area = (base × height) / 2 = (6 × 8) / 2 = 48 / 2 = 24 cm².
questions.hintText: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

questions.question: A simple lever has an effort arm of 4 meters and a load arm of 1 meter. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage of a lever = Effort Arm / Load Arm = 4 m / 1 m = 4.
questions.hintText: Divide the effort arm length by the load arm length.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12... Multiples of 6: 6, 12... The smallest common multiple is 12.
questions.hintText: Find the smallest number that can be divided by both 4 and 6 without remainder.

questions.question: Which atmospheric gas is the most abundant by volume in Earth's air (~78%)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere, followed by oxygen at ~21%.
questions.hintText: This gas is a key ingredient of plant fertilizer.

questions.question: In Python, what is the result of the expression `(5 > 3) and (2 > 10)`?
questions.explanation: 5 > 3 is True, but 2 > 10 is False. In boolean AND, True and False produces False.
questions.hintText: Both conditions must be true for AND to evaluate to True.

questions.question: A cyclist travels 30 km in 40 minutes. What is their average speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour. Speed = 30 / (2/3) = 30 × 3 / 2 = 45 km/h.
questions.hintText: Convert 40 minutes to hours (2/3 hr), then speed = distance / time.

questions.question: Why does Earth experience four distinct seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter)?
questions.optionsString: Earth's distance from the Sun changes dramatically|Earth's rotational axis is tilted by ~23.5 degrees|The Sun burns hotter during July and August|The Moon pulls Earth's climate bands
questions.explanation: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt causes different hemispheres to receive sunlight at different angles as it orbits the Sun.
questions.hintText: Why is it summer in the north while it is winter in the south at the same time?

questions.question: In a regular hexagon, what is the measure of each interior angle in degrees?
questions.hintText: The angles of a polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°. All 6 here are equal.

questions.question: In Python, x starts at 1 and the loop `while x < 10: x *= 2` runs until it stops. What is x afterwards?
questions.explanation: x starts at 1, then becomes 2, 4, 8 (8 < 10 is true, so it doubles again) and 16. Now 16 < 10 is false, so the loop stops with x = 16.
questions.hintText: Keep doubling x. The loop stops when x is no longer below 10.

questions.question: A cube has surface area of 150 cm². What is the volume of this cube in cm³?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces: 6a² = 150 => a² = 25 => a = 5 cm. Volume = a³ = 5³ = 125 cm³.
questions.hintText: Find the side length a first: 6 × a² = 150.

questions.question: When white light passes through a glass triangular prism, which color refracts (bends) the MOST?
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum and refracts the most through glass.
questions.hintText: Shorter wavelength bends more. Which end of the rainbow has the shortest?

questions.question: A jacket originally priced at $80 is discounted to $64. What is the percentage discount?
questions.hintText: How many dollars were taken off? Compare that with the ORIGINAL price.

questions.question: Three identical 6-Ohm resistors are connected in PARALLEL. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 => R = 2 Ω.
questions.hintText: When n identical resistors are in parallel, equivalent R = R_single / n.

questions.question: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle like a supermarket checkout line?
questions.explanation: A Queue processes elements FIFO (First In, First Out). A Stack is LIFO.
questions.hintText: Think of a pile of plates, where the last one added is used first. This one does the reverse.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the total number of possible distinct outcome sequences?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8 outcomes (HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT).
questions.hintText: Each toss has 2 possible results. Multiply the choices for all the tosses.

questions.question: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon is the theoretical boundary where the escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
questions.hintText: The 'point of no return': cross it and you can never come back out.

questions.question: How many unique ways can 5 friends stand in a single line for a group photo (5!)?
questions.explanation: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 unique permutations.
questions.hintText: 5 choices for the first spot, then one fewer for each next spot. Multiply them all.
questions.acceptedAnswers: one hundred twenty|one hundred and twenty

packs.title: Teens & High School (14–17 yrs): Exam & IQ Booster
packs.subtitle: Pythagorean geometry, syllogisms, Newton's laws, binary math & logarithms
packs.author: QuizLock Olympiad Prep

questions.question: If a right triangle has legs a = 5 and b = 12, what is the hypotenuse c?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean Theorem: c = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.
questions.hintText: Use a² + b² = c², then take a square root.

questions.question: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. What follows logically?
questions.optionsString: Copper conducts electricity|All conductors are copper|Copper is an insulator|Some metals do not conduct
questions.explanation: By universal instantiation (Modus Ponens): if every member of set M has property E, and C ∈ M, then C has property E.
questions.hintText: Apply the rule for all metals to copper.

questions.question: What net force F (in Newtons) is required to accelerate a 5 kg mass at 4 m/s²?
questions.explanation: By Newton's Second Law: F = m × a = 5 kg × 4 m/s² = 20 N.
questions.hintText: Use Newton's second law: force = mass × acceleration.

questions.question: Choose the best synonym for 'PRAGMATIC':
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a practical way.
questions.hintText: Picture someone who picks whatever actually works, whatever the theory says.

questions.question: What is the decimal (base-10) value of the 4-bit binary number 1010₂?
questions.hintText: Read the bits from the right as 1, 2, 4, 8 and add the places that hold a 1.

questions.question: What is log₂(256)? (To what power must 2 be raised to equal 256?)
questions.explanation: Since 2⁸ = 256, log₂(256) = 8.
questions.hintText: Keep doubling 2 and count how many 2s you multiply to reach 256.

questions.question: For any angle θ, what is the exact value of sin²(θ) + cos²(θ)?
questions.explanation: The fundamental Pythagorean trigonometric identity states sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.
questions.hintText: Picture the point (cos θ, sin θ) on the unit circle and apply Pythagoras.

questions.question: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, yielding a neutral pH of exactly 7.
questions.hintText: Acids have a low pH and bases a high pH; neutral sits exactly between them.

questions.question: What is the value of log₁₀(1000)?
questions.hintText: Count the zeros: 10 to what power gives 1000?

questions.question: How many bits are in one standard Byte?
questions.explanation: 1 Byte is defined as exactly 8 bits (capable of representing 256 distinct values).
questions.hintText: One byte can store any number from 0 to 255. How many binary digits does that take?

questions.question: For ax² + bx + c = 0, what does a discriminant D = b² - 4ac > 0 indicate about the roots?
questions.optionsString: No real roots (two complex roots)|Two distinct real roots|Exactly one real root (multiplicity 2)|All roots are zero
questions.explanation: When D > 0, the quadratic formula yields two distinct real solutions.
questions.hintText: Put a positive D into x = (−b ± √D) / 2a and count the different results.

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy (in Joules) of an 8 kg projectile moving at 10 m/s (E = ½mv²)?
questions.hintText: Square only the speed, and don't forget the ½.

questions.question: What is the magnitude (length) of 2D vector v = (3, 4)?
questions.hintText: Use the Pythagorean theorem: √(x² + y²).

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 170 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is its wavelength λ?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 340 m/s / 170 Hz = 2.0 meters.
questions.hintText: Wavelength is the wave speed divided by the frequency.

questions.question: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number 0x1F?
questions.hintText: The left digit counts in sixteens, and the hex digit F is worth 15.

questions.question: If log₂(x) + log₂(4) = 3, what is x?
questions.hintText: log(a) + log(b) = log(ab), so log₂(4x) = 3.

questions.question: Which device transforms electrical energy into mechanical rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical motion using Lorentz forces.
questions.hintText: Think of what spins a washing-machine drum or the wheels of an electric car.

questions.question: How many combinations of 3 books can be chosen from a shelf of 5 books (C(5, 3))?
questions.hintText: Picking 3 books to take is the same as picking the 2 books to leave behind.

questions.question: According to De Morgan's Law, what is NOT (A AND B) equivalent to?
questions.optionsString: (NOT A) AND (NOT B)|(NOT A) OR (NOT B)|NOT (A OR B)|A OR B
questions.explanation: De Morgan's first law: ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ (¬A) ∨ (¬B).
questions.hintText: Check with a truth table: try A = true, B = false in each option.

questions.question: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius (the temperature at which thermal motion ceases)?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 Kelvin) corresponds to -273.15 °C.
questions.hintText: Kelvin and Celsius degrees are the same size; only the starting point differs.

questions.question: What is the infinite sum S = 2 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...?
questions.explanation: Formula S = a / (1 - r) with initial term a = 2 and common ratio r = 1/2: S = 2 / (1 - 0.5) = 4.
questions.hintText: Geometric series: sum = first term ÷ (1 − common ratio). Find the ratio first.

questions.question: If a radioactive isotope has a half-life of 4 hours, what fraction remains after 12 hours?
questions.explanation: 12 hours = 3 half-lives. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.
questions.hintText: Count how many 4-hour half-lives fit in 12 hours, then halve once for each.

questions.question: What is the area of a trapezoid with parallel bases 8 cm and 12 cm, and height 6 cm?
questions.hintText: Area = average of the two parallel bases × height.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching in a Balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL or Red-Black)?
questions.explanation: Because the height of a balanced tree with n nodes is bounded by log₂(n), search takes O(log n).
questions.hintText: Each step cuts the remaining search space in half.

questions.question: What optical phenomenon explains why diamonds exhibit such brilliant sparkle and fire?
questions.explanation: Diamonds have a high refractive index (2.42) and small critical angle (~24.4°), trapping light via total internal reflection.
questions.hintText: What does light do at the inner wall of a glass block when it hits at a big angle?

questions.question: What is the instantaneous rate of change (derivative dy/dx) of y = x² at the point where x = 1?
questions.explanation: The power rule gives dy/dx = 2x. Evaluated at x = 1, the slope is 2(1) = 2.
questions.hintText: Use the power rule d/dx xⁿ = n·xⁿ⁻¹, then plug in x = 1.

questions.question: According to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence equation E = mc², what does 'c' represent?
questions.optionsString: Speed of light in vacuum|Speed of sound|Capacitance|Coulomb's constant
questions.explanation: In E = mc², c is the speed of light in vacuum (~3 × 10⁸ m/s).
questions.hintText: Check the units: a joule is kg·m²/s², so what kind of quantity is c?
questions.acceptedAnswers: speed of light|the speed of light|light speed|velocity of light

questions.question: How many total possible outcomes exist when rolling three standard 6-sided dice simultaneously (6³)?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 faces: 6 × 6 × 6 = 6³ = 216 distinct outcomes.
questions.hintText: Each die has 6 outcomes whatever the others show, so multiply them.

questions.question: What is the result of the bitwise XOR operation `5 ^ 3` (in binary: `101₂ ^ 011₂`)?
questions.hintText: XOR gives 1 only where the two bits differ; go column by column.

questions.question: According to Bernoulli's principle, when the velocity of a flowing fluid increases, what happens to its static pressure?
questions.optionsString: It decreases|It increases|It remains constant|It becomes negative
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that an increase in fluid speed occurs simultaneously with a decrease in static pressure.
questions.hintText: Think how a plane wing gets lift: air moves faster over its curved top.

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling a sum of 8 with two fair 6-sided dice?
questions.explanation: Pairs summing to 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) — exactly 5 combinations out of 36.
questions.hintText: Count ordered pairs, so (2, 6) and (6, 2) are different outcomes.

questions.question: What does the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle state cannot be measured simultaneously with arbitrary precision?
questions.optionsString: Mass and charge|Position and momentum|Temperature and pressure|Velocity and acceleration
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's principle states Δx × Δp ≥ ℏ/2; exact position and momentum cannot both be known simultaneously.
questions.hintText: Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ/2 — think about what the letters x and p stand for.

questions.question: What is 17 mod 5?
questions.explanation: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2, so the remainder (17 mod 5) is 2.
questions.hintText: mod means remainder after division: how many whole 5s fit in 17?

packs.title: IQ 140+ Pattern & Matrix Challenge
packs.subtitle: Fibonacci & cubic series, exponential growth riddles, truth-lie paradoxes & combinatorics
packs.author: QuizLock Logic Lab

questions.question: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... What is the next number in this sequence?
questions.explanation: Each Fibonacci term is the sum of the two preceding terms: F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2) = 8 + 13 = 21.
questions.hintText: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it.

questions.question: Look at the sequence of cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, ... What is the 5th term (5³)?
questions.explanation: The sequence is n³: 1³=1, 2³=8, 3³=27, 4³=64, and 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
questions.hintText: The nth term is n × n × n.

questions.question: A patch of lily pads doubles in size every day. If it covers the entire lake on Day 30, on which day did it cover HALF the lake?
questions.explanation: Because the patch doubles every single day, one day before reaching 100% (Day 30) it covered 50% — on Day 29!
questions.hintText: Run the doubling in reverse: each earlier day has half the area.

questions.question: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of an analog clock rotate in 2.5 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes 360° in 60 minutes (6° per minute). In 2.5 minutes: 2.5 × 6° = 15°.
questions.hintText: A full turn is 360° per 60 minutes. Find the degrees per minute first.

questions.question: Gold is in 1 of 3 boxes. Box A says: 'The gold is in here.' Box B says: 'The gold is not in here.' Box C says: 'The gold is not in Box A.' If ONLY ONE label is true, where is the gold?
questions.explanation: If gold is in Box B: A is false, B is false, and C ('not in A') is true — exactly 1 true statement!
questions.hintText: Try the gold in each box in turn and count how many statements are true.

questions.question: How many distinct 4-digit PIN codes can be formed using the digits {1, 2, 3, 4} without repeating any digit (4!)?
questions.explanation: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 unique permutations.
questions.hintText: Choose the first digit in 4 ways, then count the choices for each next digit.

questions.question: What is the only even prime number in mathematics?
questions.explanation: 2 is the only even prime number, because every other even number is divisible by 2.
questions.hintText: A prime has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. Test the options.

questions.question: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... What is the 6th term?
questions.explanation: The sequence of perfect squares: n² => 6² = 36.
questions.hintText: Compare each term with its position: 1st = 1×1, 2nd = 2×2...

questions.question: A standard six-sided die has opposite sides that always sum to what number?
questions.explanation: On any standard gaming die, opposite faces always sum to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4).
questions.hintText: Look at a real die and add the dots on two opposite faces.

questions.question: A standard cube has 6 faces and 8 vertices. How many edges does it have?
questions.explanation: By Euler's polyhedron formula V - E + F = 2: 8 - E + 6 = 2 => E = 12 edges.
questions.hintText: Euler's formula links the counts: V - E + F = 2.

questions.question: In a dark room with 12 black socks and 12 blue socks, what is the minimum socks you must draw to GUARANTEE a matching pair?
questions.explanation: There are 2 colors (pigeonholes). Drawing 3 socks guarantees at least two of the same color.
questions.hintText: Imagine the worst luck: how many draws can you make without a pair?

questions.question: What number comes next in the sequence: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, ...?
questions.explanation: Differences are consecutive odd numbers: +3, +5, +7, +9, +11, +13. 37 + 13 = 50 (or n² + 1).
questions.hintText: Compare each term with a perfect square: 2 vs 1, 5 vs 4, 10 vs 9.

questions.question: On an island where knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie, person A says 'I am a knave'. Can such a person exist?
questions.optionsString: Yes, A is a knave|No, it is a paradox|Yes, A is a knight|Yes, but only at night
questions.explanation: A knight cannot say it (it would be a lie), and a knave cannot say it (it would be true). It's an impossible paradox.
questions.hintText: Knights always tell the truth, knaves always lie. Test each type.

questions.question: 3, 5, 9, 15, 23, 33, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: Differences are +2, +4, +6, +8, +10. Next difference is +12 => 33 + 12 = 45.
questions.hintText: Look at the gaps between neighbouring terms. Do they follow a pattern?

questions.question: A 3×3×3 large cube is painted red on the outside and cut into 27 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have RED PAINT ON EXACTLY TWO FACES?
questions.explanation: Cubes with 2 painted faces lie along the edges (excluding corners): 12 edges × 1 = 12 cubes.
questions.hintText: Corners, edge pieces, face centres, core: which type shows two painted faces?

questions.question: A 3×3×3 cube is painted red on the outside and cut into 27 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have RED PAINT ON EXACTLY THREE FACES?
questions.explanation: Only the 8 corner cubes have 3 painted faces.
questions.hintText: How many corners does a cube have?

questions.question: Look at the triplets: (2, 3, 13), (3, 4, 25), (4, 5, 41). Following the rule a² + b² = c, what is the third value for (5, 6, ?)?
questions.hintText: Square each number first, then add the two results.

questions.question: A boat travels 12 km downstream in 1 hour and returns upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the river current?
questions.explanation: v_down = 12 km/h, v_up = 6 km/h. Current speed = (v_down - v_up) / 2 = (12 - 6) / 2 = 3 km/h.
questions.hintText: Half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds.
questions.acceptedAnswers: 3 km per hour|3 kilometres per hour|3 kilometers per hour

questions.question: Three friends (Alice, Bob, Carol) wear red, blue, green hats. Alice is not wearing red. Carol is wearing green. What color is Alice's hat?
questions.explanation: Carol wears green. Red is left for Bob because Alice cannot wear red. Thus Alice wears blue.
questions.hintText: Cross out Carol's colour, then use the clue about Alice's hat.

questions.question: A Mersenne number has form 2^p - 1. Which of the following is a Mersenne prime?
questions.explanation: 2⁷ - 1 = 128 - 1 = 127 is a prime number. 15=3×5, 63=7×9, 511=7×73 are composite.
questions.hintText: Test each option for small factors such as 3, 5 and 7.

questions.question: A family has two children. You are told that AT LEAST ONE is a boy. What is the probability that BOTH are boys?
questions.explanation: Possible gender pairs: {BB, BG, GB, GG}. Knowing at least one is a boy eliminates GG, leaving {BB, BG, GB}. Only BB has both boys: 1/3.
questions.hintText: List the equally likely boy/girl orders, then strike out those the clue rules out.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand of a clock at exactly 3:15?
questions.explanation: At 3:15, the minute hand is at 90°. The hour hand has moved 15 min × 0.5°/min = 7.5° past 90°. The angle is 7.5°.
questions.hintText: The hour hand creeps on all the time: how far per minute at 30° per hour?

questions.question: What is the maximum number of coins among which you can always find 1 heavier counterfeit coin using 4 weighings on a balance scale?
questions.explanation: Each balance scale comparison yields 3 outcomes (left heavier, equal, right heavier). 3⁴ = 81 coins.
questions.hintText: Each weighing has 3 outcomes. How many do 4 weighings give together?

questions.question: If all Zorks are Flips, and no Flips are Glims, which conclusion MUST be true?
questions.optionsString: Some Glims are Zorks|All Glims are Flips|No Zorks are Glims|All Zorks are Glims
questions.explanation: Since the set of Zorks is entirely inside Flips, and Flips has zero intersection with Glims, Zorks has zero intersection with Glims.
questions.hintText: Sketch the three groups as circles: can Zorks reach Glims?

questions.question: An octahedron has 8 triangular faces and 6 vertices. What is its dual Platonic solid?
questions.explanation: The dual swaps faces and vertices: 8 vertices and 6 faces corresponds to the Cube.
questions.hintText: A dual swaps the numbers of faces and vertices. Compare with each solid.

questions.question: If statement 'A implies B' is TRUE, what other statement is GUARANTEED to be true?
questions.optionsString: NOT B implies NOT A (Contrapositive)|B implies A (Converse)|NOT A implies NOT B (Inverse)|A AND B are both true
questions.explanation: The contrapositive (¬B → ¬A) is logically equivalent to the original conditional (A → B).
questions.hintText: Take 'if it rains, the street is wet'. What follows from a dry street?
questions.acceptedAnswers: Contrapositive|If not B then not A

questions.question: In a standard 9×9 Sudoku grid, what is the sum of numbers 1 through 9 in ANY completed row, column, or 3×3 box?
questions.explanation: The sum of integers 1 to 9 is n(n+1)/2 = 9 × 10 / 2 = 45.
questions.hintText: Each row uses 1 to 9 once: pair 1 with 9, 2 with 8, and so on.

questions.question: A barber in a town shaves only those men who DO NOT shave themselves. Does the barber shave himself?
questions.optionsString: Yes, he must shave himself|It is Russell's Paradox|No, his apprentice shaves him|He must have a full beard
questions.explanation: Russell's Paradox: If he shaves himself, he breaks the rule. If he doesn't shave himself, he must shave himself.
questions.hintText: Assume he shaves himself, then assume he doesn't, and check each against the rule.

questions.question: Three prisoners stand in a line facing forward: C (at the back) sees B and A, B sees only A, and A sees nobody. Their hats come from a set of 2 black and 3 white. C sees a black hat on A and a white hat on B. Can C deduce his own hat color?
questions.optionsString: No, C has no information|Yes, C has a black hat|Yes, C has a white hat|Only if B speaks first
questions.explanation: C sees A black and B white, so 1 black and 2 white hats remain unseen and C's own hat could be either colour. B sees only A, so he cannot work out his own hat either, and his silence tells C nothing.
questions.hintText: Count how many hats of each colour C cannot see.

questions.question: What is the number of derangements of 3 items (permutations where NO element appears in its original position)?
questions.hintText: List all arrangements of A, B, C and cross out any with a letter in its own place.

questions.question: 2 -> 6, 3 -> 12, 4 -> 20, 5 -> 30. What does 7 map to under the rule n(n + 1)?
questions.hintText: Replace n with 7 in both places, then multiply.

questions.question: How many distinct subsets does a finite set of 7 elements contain (including empty set and itself)?
questions.explanation: The power set of a set with n elements has 2^n subsets: 2⁷ = 128.
questions.hintText: Each element is either in a subset or out: 2 choices per element.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of moves required to solve ANY scrambled 3×3×3 Rubik's Cube in half-turn metric?
questions.explanation: Proven mathematically in 2010 using supercomputers, 'God's Number' for the 3×3×3 cube is exactly 20 moves.
questions.hintText: It is called God's Number and was settled by a 2010 computer search.

packs.title: Junior Scholars (7–9 yrs): Fun Math & Brain Riddles
packs.subtitle: Grades 2–4 multiplication, square perimeters, coins, clock puzzles & animal riddles
packs.author: QuizLock Junior Academy

questions.question: One spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 7 spiders have altogether? (7 × 8)
questions.explanation: 7 groups of 8 equals 56 (7 × 8 = 56). Fun memory trick: 5, 6, 7, 8 → 56 = 7 × 8!
questions.hintText: Try 7 × 4 first, then double the result.

questions.question: A square garden has 4 equal sides. Each side is 6 meters long. What is the perimeter (total distance around) in meters?
questions.explanation: The perimeter of a square is P = 4 × a. With side a = 6 m, P = 4 × 6 = 24 meters.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 equal sides together: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 (or 4 × 6).

questions.question: How many minutes are there in 1 and a half hours (1.5 hours)?
questions.explanation: 1 hour (60 min) + half an hour (30 min) = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes.
questions.hintText: How many minutes are in 1 hour? And in half an hour? Then put them together.

questions.question: You have a 100-cent (1 Dollar) coin and buy a sticker pack for 65 cents. How many cents change do you get back?
questions.explanation: 100 − 65 = 35 cents change (because 65 + 35 = 100).
questions.hintText: Subtract 65 from 100: 100 − 60 = 40, and 40 − 5 = ?

questions.question: Mia sees 3 ducks and 2 cows in a meadow. Each duck has 2 legs and each cow has 4 legs. How many legs are there in total?
questions.explanation: 3 ducks × 2 legs = 6 legs. 2 cows × 4 legs = 8 legs. Total: 6 + 8 = 14 legs!
questions.hintText: Count the duck legs and the cow legs separately, then put them together.

questions.question: When Leo was 6 years old, his little sister Anna was half his age (3). Now Leo is 10 years old. How old is Anna now?
questions.optionsString: 5 years old|7 years old|8 years old|6 years old
questions.explanation: Anna is 3 years younger than Leo (6 − 3 = 3). When Leo is 10, Anna is 10 − 3 = 7 years old!
questions.hintText: Find out how many years older Leo is. That gap never changes.

questions.question: What is 6 × 4?
questions.explanation: 6 groups of 4 equals 24 (6 × 4 = 24).
questions.hintText: Double 6, then double the result.

questions.question: How many hours are there in one complete day and night?
questions.explanation: One full Earth day has 24 hours.
questions.hintText: A clock face shows 12 hours, and the short hand goes around it twice a day.

questions.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A pentagon is a polygon with exactly 5 sides and 5 angles.
questions.hintText: Draw a simple house shape with a pointy roof and count its sides.

questions.question: What is 9 × 5?
questions.hintText: Count by fives and use your fingers to keep track of nine jumps.

questions.question: If you have two 25-cent coins (quarters), how many cents do you have in total?
questions.explanation: 25¢ + 25¢ = 50¢ (half a dollar).
questions.hintText: Try 20 + 20 first, then add the two 5s.

questions.question: What is 5 + 5 + 5?
questions.explanation: Three 5s equal 3 × 5 = 15.
questions.hintText: 5 + 5 = 10, then add 5 more.

questions.question: How many days are in one week?
questions.explanation: A week consists of 7 days: Monday through Sunday.
questions.hintText: Count Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is an EVEN number (ends in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8)?
questions.explanation: 30 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 2 and even.
questions.hintText: Even numbers can be split into two equal whole halves.

questions.question: What is 4 × 9?
questions.hintText: Double 9, then double the result again.

questions.question: There are 8 ducks swimming. 7 more fly in to join them. How many ducks are there now?
questions.explanation: 8 + 7 = 15 ducks.
questions.hintText: First make 10: how many does 8 need? Then add the rest.

questions.question: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) = 2 × (5 + 3) = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.
questions.hintText: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. Add all four.

questions.question: What is 7 × 6?
questions.hintText: Do 7 × 5 first, then add one more 7.

questions.question: 5, 10, 15, 20, ... What is the missing number?
questions.explanation: Adding 5 each step: 20 + 5 = 25.
questions.hintText: Look at how much the numbers go up each time, then take one more step.

questions.question: You have 18 candies to share equally among 3 friends. How many candies does each friend get?
questions.explanation: 18 divided by 3 is 6 (18 ÷ 3 = 6).

questions.question: One full carton holds 12 eggs (one dozen). How many eggs are in 2 cartons?
questions.hintText: Double 12: 12 + 12.

questions.question: What is 9 × 7?
questions.hintText: Do 10 × 7 first, then take away one 7.

questions.question: Max had 45 toy bricks. He used 25 of them to build a tower. How many bricks does he have left?
questions.explanation: 45 - 25 = 20 bricks.
questions.hintText: Subtract the tens first, then the ones.

questions.question: What is half of 1/2 of an apple?
questions.explanation: Half of a half is 1/4 (one quarter).
questions.hintText: Cut the half-apple into 2 equal pieces. How many of those fit in a whole apple?

questions.question: What is 8 × 9?
questions.hintText: Do 8 × 10 first, then take away one 8.

questions.question: A movie starts at 4:15 PM and ends at 4:50 PM. How many minutes long was the movie?
questions.explanation: 50 - 15 = 35 minutes.
questions.hintText: Subtract 15 from 50.

questions.question: What is 8 × 8?
questions.hintText: Double 8, double that, then double it once more.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides of 9 cm each. What is its perimeter?
questions.hintText: Add 9 three times: 9 + 9 + 9.

questions.question: A toy robot weighs as much as 2 toy cars. If 1 toy car weighs 3 kg, how much does the robot weigh?
questions.explanation: 2 × 3 kg = 6 kg.
questions.hintText: Multiply 2 by 3.

questions.question: In the number 472, what is the value of the digit 4?
questions.explanation: The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, representing 400.
questions.hintText: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds. Which place is the 4 in?

questions.question: Two years ago, Emma was 8 years old. How old will she be 4 years from NOW?
questions.explanation: Two years ago she was 8, so now she is 8 + 2 = 10. In 4 years: 10 + 4 = 14.
questions.hintText: Find her age today first. Then count forward from there.

questions.question: If you divide 17 marbles equally among 4 bags, how many marbles are left over?
questions.explanation: 17 = (4 × 4) + 1. Each bag gets 4 marbles, and 1 marble is left over.
questions.hintText: Give each bag 4 marbles, then count the marbles still in your hand.

questions.question: How many centimeters (cm) are in 1 meter?
questions.explanation: 1 meter = 100 centimeters.
questions.hintText: Picture a meter stick and count along it by tens, up to the end.

packs.title: Junior Scientists (7–9 yrs): Nature, Space & Matter
packs.subtitle: Water states (H₂O), Solar System planets, magnets, plant photosynthesis & rainbows
packs.author: QuizLock Junior Academy

questions.question: When liquid water (H₂O) cools down to 0 °C (32 °F), it freezes into a solid. What do we call solid water?
questions.explanation: At 0 °C, liquid water (H₂O) freezes into solid ice crystals!
questions.hintText: Think of what you put in a cold drink or skate on in winter!

questions.question: Every magnet has a North (N) pole and a South (S) pole. What happens when you bring a North pole close to a South pole?
questions.optionsString: They pull together (attract)|They push apart (repel)|Nothing happens|They spin in circles
questions.explanation: Opposite magnetic poles (North and South) attract each other, while same poles (N–N or S–S) push apart!
questions.hintText: N and S are opposite poles. Opposite poles act differently from matching poles (N and N).

questions.question: Which planet is the 3rd planet from the Sun and our home with liquid oceans of H₂O?
questions.explanation: Order from the Sun: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars. Earth is the 3rd planet!
questions.hintText: Say the planets in order from the Sun and stop at number 3.

questions.question: Plants use sunlight, water (H₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) to make food and release which gas that we breathe?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, green plants take in CO₂ and H₂O and release fresh oxygen (O₂) into the air!
questions.hintText: Your body and a burning candle both need this gas from the air.

questions.question: What happens when white sunlight shines through tiny raindrops in the sky?
questions.optionsString: It splits into 7 rainbow colors|It turns pitch black|It freezes into hail|It makes thunder
questions.explanation: Raindrops act like tiny glass prisms, bending white sunlight into the 7 colors of the rainbow!
questions.hintText: Think about what appears in the sky when the sun comes out during a rain shower.

questions.question: How many major planets orbit the Sun in our Solar System (from Mercury out to Neptune)?
questions.explanation: There are 8 major planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
questions.hintText: Count the rocky planets near the Sun, then the giant planets farther out.

questions.question: Which organ in your chest pumps blood through your entire body all day and night?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps oxygen-rich blood through your arteries and veins.
questions.hintText: It beats steadily: thump-thump, thump-thump.

questions.question: Which part of a plant grows downward into the soil to absorb water and minerals?
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant in soil and absorb water and nutrients.
questions.hintText: Think of what holds a big tree firmly in the ground when the wind blows.

questions.question: Which sense organ allows you to hear music and sounds?
questions.explanation: Ears capture sound vibrations in the air and send signals to your brain.
questions.hintText: Think of what you cover when a noise is too loud.

questions.question: Which of these animals is NOCTURNAL (active mainly at night)?
questions.explanation: Owls hunt at night and sleep during the day, making them nocturnal.
questions.hintText: Most of these are busy by day. Which one is awake while you sleep?

questions.question: What falls from clouds as precipitation during cold winter when water freezes?
questions.explanation: When water vapor freezes into ice crystals in cold air, it falls as snow.
questions.hintText: Think of what makes the ground white and fluffy in winter.

questions.question: What happens when you drop an apple from your hand?
questions.optionsString: It floats upward|It falls down toward Earth|It turns sideways|It disappears
questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational force pulls all objects down toward the ground.
questions.hintText: Let go of a toy: which way does it go?

questions.question: What is the process called when liquid puddle water heats up in the sun and turns into invisible vapor in the air?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the transition of liquid water into invisible gas (water vapor).
questions.hintText: Think of wet washing drying in the sun: the water floats away into the air.

questions.question: How long does it take for Earth to complete ONE full orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Earth takes about 365.25 days (one full year) to orbit the Sun once.
questions.hintText: How long until your birthday comes around again?

questions.question: Animals with backbones (spines) are called vertebrates. Which of these is an INVERTEBRATE (no bones)?
questions.explanation: Jellyfish have soft bodies with no skeleton or backbone (invertebrates).
questions.hintText: Think of which one is soft and wobbly all over, with nothing hard inside.

questions.question: Why do objects cast shadows on the ground on a sunny day?
questions.optionsString: Light goes straight and the object blocks it|The ground absorbs all the sunlight|The object gives off cold darkness|The Sun switches off behind it
questions.explanation: Light rays travel in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the rays, an unlit shadow forms behind it.
questions.hintText: Hold your hand in front of a lamp: what does your hand do to the light?

questions.question: Which planet is nicknamed the 'Red Planet' because of its rusty iron-rich soil?
questions.explanation: Mars has abundant iron oxide (rust) on its surface, giving it a distinct reddish appearance.
questions.hintText: The 4th planet from the Sun.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat ONLY plants (like rabbits and cows)?
questions.explanation: Herbivores (from Latin herba = plant) feed exclusively on plant matter.
questions.hintText: Look at the start of each word. One sounds like 'herb', a green plant.

questions.question: Why does the Moon appear to change shape (phases: crescent, half, full) from Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon physically grows and shrinks|We see different parts of its sunlit half|Earth's clouds cover parts of the Moon|The Sun turns off one side of the Moon
questions.explanation: As the Moon circles Earth, our viewpoint of the half illuminated by the Sun changes continually.
questions.hintText: Shine a lamp on a ball and walk around it. Does the lit part look the same?

questions.question: What do we call it when an animal blends into its surroundings (like a chameleon or arctic fox)?
questions.explanation: Camouflage allows animals to disguise their appearance to hide from predators or prey.
questions.hintText: Think of playing hide-and-seek in clothes that match the wall.

questions.question: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR (allows electricity to flow through it)?
questions.explanation: Metals like copper have free electrons and are excellent electrical conductors.
questions.hintText: Think of what a charger cable is made of inside, under its soft cover.

questions.question: What are fossils?
questions.optionsString: Rare rocks formed in space|Remains of ancient life kept in rock|Pieces of fallen meteorites|Frozen water underground
questions.explanation: Fossils are the mineralized remains of ancient plants, animals, or dinosaur bones preserved in stone.
questions.hintText: How scientists study dinosaurs that lived millions of years ago.

questions.question: Which biome has very little rainfall, extreme hot daytime temperatures, and cactus plants?
questions.explanation: Deserts receive less than 25 cm of precipitation annually and support specialized flora like cacti.
questions.hintText: Think of where a camel feels at home.

questions.question: How is sound created?
questions.optionsString: By very bright light|By very cold air|By something that vibrates|By strong magnets
questions.explanation: Sound is produced when a vibrating object causes pressure waves in the surrounding air, liquid, or solid.
questions.hintText: Put your fingers on your throat and hum. What do you feel?

questions.question: Which invisible force pulls rain, rivers, and all objects down to the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force that Earth exerts on all masses.
questions.hintText: Jump as high as you can: what brings you back down?

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton consists of 206 distinct bones.
questions.hintText: Babies have about 300 bones, but many join together as you grow up.
questions.acceptedAnswers: two hundred six|two hundred and six

questions.question: What is the green pigment in plant leaves that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light from the Sun and gives leaves their green color.
questions.hintText: Think of it as the plant's tiny solar panels.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its massive, beautiful system of rings made of ice and rock particles?
questions.explanation: Saturn is the gas giant renowned for its spectacular, wide ring system.
questions.hintText: Count outward from the Sun: it is the 6th planet.

questions.question: What causes thunder during a thunderstorm?
questions.optionsString: Clouds crashing together like rocks|Lightning heats air so fast that it bursts outward|Rain falling too fast|Wind shaking the mountains
questions.explanation: Lightning heats the surrounding air channel to ~30,000 °C in milliseconds; the rapid explosive expansion creates thunder.
questions.hintText: A popping balloon makes a bang because air moves suddenly.

questions.question: How do bats navigate and find tiny insects in pitch darkness?
questions.optionsString: Echolocation (listening to echoes)|Seeing the heat of insects|Smelling insects from miles away|Following a built-in compass
questions.explanation: Bats use echolocation: high-frequency ultrasound calls bounce off targets and reveal their exact location.
questions.hintText: Shout in a big empty hall or tunnel: what comes back to your ears?

questions.question: What is molten liquid rock called while it is STILL underground inside a volcano?
questions.explanation: Underground it is called magma; once it erupts onto the surface it is called lava.
questions.hintText: Once it pours out into the open air, it gets a new name.

questions.question: What covers approximately 71% of the entire surface of planet Earth?
questions.explanation: Oceans cover roughly 71% of Earth's surface, which is why Earth is called the 'Blue Marble'.
questions.hintText: Spin a globe: which kind of area do you see most?

questions.question: What gas do humans and animals exhale into the air that green plants absorb?
questions.explanation: Animals breathe in O₂ and exhale CO₂; plants use CO₂ in photosynthesis to generate oxygen.
questions.hintText: You breathe this gas out, and fizzy drinks have it in their bubbles.

packs.title: Junior Chess, Word Heroes & Kid Coding (7–9 yrs)
packs.subtitle: 1-move Junior Chess mates on the 2D board, vocabulary opposites & robot repeat loops
